questions.question: A textbook has a total of 662 pages. It is divided into two parts. The second part of the book has 52 pages less than the first part. How many pages are there in the first part of the book?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total pages in the textbook = 662

The second part of the book has 52 pages less than the first part.

**Formula Used:**

Let the number of pages in the first part be x.

Number of pages in the second part = x - 52

Total pages = Pages in the first part + Pages in the second part

**Calculation:**

x + (x - 52) = 662

⇒ 2x - 52 = 662

⇒ 2x = 662 + 52

⇒ 2x = 714

⇒ x = 714 / 2

⇒ x = 357

**The number of pages in the first part of the book is 357.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a false weight on which 984 gm is written, but actually weighs lesser. Using this false weight, the shopkeeper makes a gain of 23%. The actual measure of the weight used is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The shopkeeper uses a false weight on which 984 gm is written.

The false weight actually weighs lesser than 984 gm.

The shopkeeper makes a gain of 23%.

**Formula Used:**

Gain Percentage = (False weight / Actual weight - 1) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the actual measure of the weight used be x gm.

According to the given information:

23 = (984 / x - 1) × 100

⇒ 23 / 100 = 984 / x - 1

⇒ 0.23 = 984 / x - 1

⇒ 984 / x = 1.23

⇒ x = 984 / 1.23

⇒ x = 800 gm

**The actual measure of the weight used is 800 gm.**

questions.question: If 9 lines of a print, in a column of a book, contain 36 words, how many words will a column of 51 lines contain?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

9 lines contain 36 words.

**Formula Used:**

Number of words = (Number of lines) × (Words per line)

**Calculation:**

Words per line = 36 / 9

Words per line = 4

Number of words in 51 lines = 51 × 4

⇒ Number of words in 51 lines = 204

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 2. Their LCM and HCF are 24 and 4, respectively. The greater of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers = 3 : 2

LCM = 24

HCF = 4

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the two numbers be 3x and 2x.

Product of the numbers = 3x × 2x = 6x²

Given: Product of the numbers = LCM × HCF = 24 × 4 = 96

⇒ 6x² = 96

⇒ x² = 96 / 6

⇒ x² = 16

⇒ x = 4

So, the two numbers are 3x = 3 × 4 = 12 and 2x = 2 × 4 = 8.

The greater of the two numbers is 12.

questions.question: If a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 4 : 1 , then a : b : c = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the common term 'b' is identical in both the given ratios, we can write the combined ratio directly without any cross-multiplication.

Given a : b = 3 : 4 and b : c = 4 : 1.

Since the value of b is exactly 4 in both parts, we just merge the corresponding values of a, b, and c side by side.

⇒ a : b : c = 3 : 4 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of a : b = 3 : 4

Ratio of b : c = 4 : 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40c7ca74f2d18f7c26f4c9f3bc2aa45011a7f3081d7b02788111a5d77c178ad6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the ratio a : b, the value representing b is 4 units.

⇒ In the ratio b : c, the value representing b is also 4 units.

⇒ Since the common linking variable 'b' has an identical value in both ratios, no further multiplication or scaling is required.

⇒ We can directly extract and equate the combined values of a, b, and c relative to each other.

⇒ a = 3, b = 4, c = 1

⇒ a : b : c = 3 : 4 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverted 'N' Method for Combining Ratios

If a : b = p : q and b : c = x : y, then a : b : c = (p × x) : (q × x) : (q × y). This trick is helpful when the middle term 'b' is completely different in both cases and needs to be equalised.

Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, and d are said to be in proportion if a : b = c : d. A very important mathematical property here is that the product of the extremes equals the product of the means: a × d = b × c.

Duplicate & Triplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given by a² : b², and the triplicate ratio of a : b is given by a³ : b³. Conversely, the sub-duplicate ratio is written as √a : √b.

Mode = 3 × Median - 2 × Mean

questions.question: A cyclist covers 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover 6 km at the same speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered = 2.5 km

Time taken = 4 minutes 10 seconds = 4 + 10/60 minutes = 4 + 1/6 minutes = 25/6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 2.5 km / (25/6 minutes)

⇒ Speed = 2.5 × (6/25) km/minute

⇒ Speed = 0.6 km/minute

To find the time to cover 6 km:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 6 km / 0.6 km/minute

⇒ Time = 10 minutes

**The cyclist will take 10 minutes to cover 6 km at the same speed.**

questions.question: An article is sold for ₹ x after offering two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on its marked price of ₹ 500. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of the article = ₹ 500

Successive discounts = 20% and 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount₁) × (1 - Discount₂)

**Calculation:**

Discount₁ = 20% = 20/100 = 0.20

Discount₂ = 15% = 15/100 = 0.15

⇒ Selling Price = 500 × (1 - 0.20) × (1 - 0.15)

⇒ Selling Price = 500 × 0.80 × 0.85

⇒ Selling Price = 500 × 0.68

⇒ Selling Price = 340

**The value of x is ₹ 340.**

questions.question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days. How many more days will 1 woman take to build that wall alone compared to the number of days 1 man will take to build the wall?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days.

6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days.

**Formula used:**

Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of a man be 'm' and of a woman be 'w'.

The total work done is the same in both cases. Therefore:

⇒ (8m + 12w) × 10 = (6m + 8w) × 14

⇒ 80m + 120w = 84m + 112w

⇒ 120w - 112w = 84m - 80m

⇒ 8w = 4m

⇒ 1m = 2w

**Find the number of days for 1 man and 1 woman to build the wall:**

From the first case: Total work = (8m + 12w) × 10

⇒ Total work = (8 × 2w + 12w) × 10 = 28w × 10 = 280w

Efficiency of 1 man = 2w, so time taken by 1 man = ​(280w)/(2w) = 140 days

Efficiency of 1 woman = w, so time taken by 1 woman = (280w)/(w) = 280 days

Difference in days = (280 - 140 = 140) days.

**∴ 1 woman will take 140 more days than 1 man to build the wall.**

questions.question: Two plumbers, X and Y, are paid a total of ₹660 per day by their employer. If X is paid 120% of the sum paid to Y, then how much is Y paid per day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of X's pay to Y's pay = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5

Total ratio parts = 6 + 5 = 11 parts

11 parts → ₹660

1 part → ₹660 ÷ 11 = ₹60

Y's pay = 5 parts = 5 × 60 = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10c2a83e6a3971ca8d55e45f87b635c8890fc1974535a35b10a00c09c068d260.png] 

**Given:**

Total pay of X and Y = ₹660 per day

X is paid 120% of the sum paid to Y.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the daily amount paid to Y be ₹y.

⇒ Daily amount paid to X = 120% of y = 1.2y

⇒ Total daily pay = X + Y

⇒ 1.2y + y = 660

⇒ 2.2y = 660

⇒ y = 660 ÷ 2.2

⇒ y = 300

⇒ The daily amount paid to Y is ₹300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rate of interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Extra Principal) × 100

questions.question: Find the median of the data 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Data: 11, 16, 33, 15, 51, 19, 71, 75, 21, 17

**Formula used:**

For ungrouped data, the median is the middle value when the data is arranged in ascending order.

If the total number of values (n) is:

Odd: Median = Value at position (n + 1) / 2

Even: Median = Average of values at positions (n/2) and (n/2 + 1)

**Calculations:**

Arrange the data in ascending order:

11, 15, 16, 17, 19, 21, 33, 51, 71, 75

Number of data points (n) = 10 (even)

Median position = Average of values at (n/2) and (n/2 + 1)

Positions = 10/2 = 5 and 10/2 + 1 = 6

Values at 5th and 6th positions: 19 and 21

Median = (19 + 21)/(2) = 20

**∴ The median of the data is 20.**
